Well, what happened? Maybe it's not broken, it could be a few things. Might be worth trying to fix instead of just tossing it and buying a new one. Did you try a different graphics card to make sure it's not the motherboard? Did you try the card in a different slot? Did you try a different monitor? Are you sure the rest of the computer is turning on? Is it just displaying a bunch of graphics artifacts? Did you change anything with your system before it went down? Can you boot off of a liveCD/USB and have the system work, ruling out the OS (at least if you only boot one os).

I had an old i7 920 and 4870 crossfire setup that wouldn't boot, but I could wiggle the cards around and it would start. I ended up laying it on its side and it was fine. I actually ended up buying a 7970 to fix it, and I was pretty annoyed when the 7970 didn't work all the time like the 4870s didn't work. Turns out it needed some wobble since the contacts in the motherboard's PCIe slots were going out.

It could be a lot of things, I don't know how much you've troubleshooted, but I've been in your position before and I've bought things to fix something, only to find I was wrong and I spent money on something that didn't fix it.
